rationale: Zero-parameter and typed legacy parameter lists are both versioned syntax.
A function call is a first-class expression.
Arguments accept arbitrary expressions in source order.
Calls carry exact declared result types.
Interpreter frames execute nested and recursive calls.
LLVM lowers expression calls with exact argument values.
Typed declarations are executable statements inside blocks.
Braced blocks explicitly carry lexical-scope identity.
Same-scope duplicates are rejected while nested shadowing is defined.
Interpreter block entry and exit own deterministic storage cleanup.
LLVM name and type lookup follows lexical scope nesting.
Goto targets resolve within the current lexical block.
Interpreter goto execution uses an explicit program-counter transfer.
LLVM predeclares lexical label blocks for conditional and unconditional forward and backward branches.
Goto cannot bypass block cleanup by escaping a lexical scope.
Goto cannot cross a local declaration lifetime boundary.
Duplicate labels have a stable source diagnostic.
Undefined labels fail before execution and lowering.
Non-void functions must return on every structured path.
Same-scope local redeclaration is deterministic and fail-closed.
Void results cannot enter value-consuming contexts.
Undefined calls fail in semantic analysis rather than lowering.
Expression arguments retain exact parameter typing.
Read statements and beta-0.2 valid syntax remain accepted.
Existing break and continue behavior remains executable.
